newsitem.title: USA: US House panel backs Export-Import Bank extension.
newsitem.headline: US House panel backs Export-Import Bank extension.

text.p: The House Banking Committee voted on Wednesday to extend the activities of the U.S. Export-Import Bank for four years.
The panel approved the measure on a voice vote. It now goes to the full House for consideration.
"Without Eximbank, American exporters would be left defenseless in the face of aggressive officially financed foreign competition," committee chairman Jim Leach said in a statement before the vote.
The independent federal agency helps exports by providing loans and guarantees for the purchase of American products, but critics have charged that its mission is one of "corporate welfare."
Three other amendments were also approved.
One requires two labor representative be appointed to the ExImbank advisory committee. Another requires the implementation of a program to increase awareness among U.S. firms of the bank's programs.
The third proposal directs the bank to try to give preference firms committed to U.S. reinvestment and job creation.
